conclusion: Two copies of the FTO obesity-associated C allele. In the characterised mechanism this allele disrupts an ARID5B repressor motif and shifts adipocyte precursors from thermogenic beige fat toward energy-storing white fat. The effect on body mass at the level of one person is small and strongly modified by diet and activity: this is a predisposition, not a diagnosis, and it says nothing about current or future weight on its own.
One copy of the FTO obesity-associated C allele and one copy of the T allele. The predisposition is intermediate between the two homozygous genotypes and small at the individual level.

No copy of the FTO obesity-associated C allele at this position. This is the more common genotype in many populations and carries no adiposity signal from this variant. It implies nothing about the many hundreds of other variants that influence body mass.
